items.headline: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia
items.blurb: Watch: The BBC's Jonathan Beale joins Ukrainian forces taking the battle below ground and out of sight of Russian drones.
items.text: For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the Kharkiv region. The BBC is the first international broadcaster to enter the pipeline where this subterranean battle is taking place. With a diameter of just over a metre there's enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line – and which are making it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance. The BBC's defence correspondent Jonathan Beale reports from near Kupyansk, where he went underground with the 13th Khartiia Operational Brigade.

items.headline: Iraq sentences six French nationals to life in prison for joining ISIL
items.blurb: Trials began in September for 47 French citizens who were transferred from Syria last year.
items.text: An Iraqi criminal court has sentenced six French nationals to life in prison for joining the ISIL (ISIS) group, state media reported. The Karkh Criminal Court delivered the sentencing on Wednesday with representatives from the French embassy in attendance, the Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported, citing Iraq’s judiciary. “With these six sentences, the total number of those convicted in this case has reached 16, all of whom are French nationals,” the judiciary said in a statement cited by INA. All but one of the 16 convicted were sentenced to life. The court sentenced one defendant to 15 years in prison last month. Trials began in September for 47 French citizens who were transferred from Syria last year and charged with belonging to the armed group, which controlled large parts of both countries between 2014 and 2017. In February, Iraq received more than 5,700 ISIL detainees from over 60 countries after the United States transferred them from Syria, following years of detention in prisons run by Kurdish-led forces. items.text: A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay , if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya. The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group. Lawyers representing Rohingya survivors say patterns of behaviour by Myanmar’s military, including killing people as they fled, show clear attempts to destroy the group during assaults on Rakhine state in 2016 and 2017. It is the role of independent judges to interpret the genocide convention. items.headline: 'The drones don't fly here' - BBC reports from Ukraine's new front line
items.blurb: Ukrainian forces are fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet tunnel in the Kharkiv region.
items.text: There's a new front in the war in Ukraine, and it is underground. For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the north-eastern Kharkiv region. With a diameter of just over a metre there is enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line – and make it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance. Going underground is now the "only option", says Zanuda, who has helped plan Ukraine's tunnel operation and calls it a new world of fighting. But, he acknowledges, it is hard. "On the surface you always have some room to manoeuvre, but here you can only engage the enemy head-on." The journey to get to this subterranean battleground in the Kharkiv region only reinforced the dangers on the ground: a high-speed move by vehicle across open fields, followed by a long march across muddy ground – accompanied by Ukrainian troops with their weapons loaded, ready to shoot down Russian drones.

items.headline: US lawmakers push to raise minimum wage to $25, end tipped pay system
items.blurb: Public support for raising the minimum wage grows, with 78 percent of voters saying it was an important election issue.
items.text: In Washington, DC, a group of lawmakers has ramped up calls to increase the United States federal minimum wage and eliminate the subminimum wage, otherwise known as the tipped wage. The group of 17 lawmakers, which includes current and newly elected House members, is calling for passage of the Living Wage For All Act, which has been languishing since it was introduced in April. The legislation’s original lead sponsors include Representative Delia Ramirez of Illinois, Representative Jesus “Chuy” Garcia, also of Illinois, and Representative Analilia Mejia of New Jersey. The bill aims to gradually raise the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour, with different timelines depending on the size of the employer. Brad Lander, a congressman-elect from Brooklyn, New York, who says he will join the bill as a co-sponsor when the next congressional session begins in January, told Al Jazeera: “Doing it federally is the right way to go. items.headline: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt
items.blurb: Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.
items.text: Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi. The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen , the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza. The disclosure raises broader questions about the EU-Egypt relationship, as Egyptian authorities face scrutiny over shrinking press freedom following the jailing and alleged torture of six journalists , the entire newsroom of Matsadaash, a factchecking and investigative platform, and the closure last month of one of the country’s last independent news outlets and conviction of its high-profile editor , Lina Attalah. items.headline: Trump shakes hands with Putin and Xi ahead of historic talks in China
items.blurb: The three leaders will meet together for the first time on Thursday during a closely-watched summit.
items.text: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met for the first time in more than a year on Wednesday, as they prepared for landmark talks in China with Xi Jinping. The US president was greeted off his plane by the Chinese leader as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting between the pair and the Russian president. After a carefully choreographed handshake and hug between Trump and Xi on the tarmac, the US president later greeted and exchanged pleasantries with Putin ahead of a reception. Trump and Putin are expected to hold one-on-one talks on the sidelines of the summit on Thursday, in which the war in Ukraine could be discussed. However the main focus during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum (Apec) will be on the US-China-Russia talks on Thursday - the first time the trio of leaders have met together in person. items.blurb: Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’ Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and…
items.text: Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’ Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”. The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country. In a statement released on Monday the five EU countries said “concrete negotiations with partner country Rwanda will begin for implementation”, saying the scheme would make “an important contribution to further curbing illegal migration, dismantling the business model of smugglers and relieving the burden on our population”. items.headline: Israeli military launches rare ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line
items.blurb: Hamas condemns the incursion, which the Israeli military says is dismantling a "terror tunnel", as a "flagrant" ceasefire violation.
items.text: Israeli ground forces have launched a rare operation in part of the central Gaza Strip outside their control, after issuing evacuation orders for residents. Witnesses said tanks advanced east of Nuseirat refugee camp and rolled onto the territory's main north to south road under the cover of artillery strikes. The Israeli military said the "targeted" operation aimed to dismantle a "terror tunnel" west of the so-called Yellow Line, which marks the more than 60% of Gaza's territory occupied by Israel. The Palestinian armed group Hamas, which controls the rest of Gaza, accused Israel of a "flagrant violation" of the October 2025 ceasefire agreement. Violence has continued in Gaza over the past 13 months, with near-daily Israeli strikes, and living conditions for the 2.1 million people there remain dire. Early on Wednesday afternoon, Israeli military body Cogat's Arabic spokesperson announced the start of the incursion and warned Palestinians living in an area north of Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camp to stay away for their own safety. items.headline: ‘Run for your safety’: The final hours before Lashkar’s Lateef Bhat was gunned down
items.text: For the last two days, a joint team of the Jammu and Kashmir Police, the Army and paramilitary forces had cordoned off several villages in Kulgam . The focus of their searches was not homes but local mosques – police had an input that Mohammad Lateef Bhat, said to be the last active local terrorist in the Valley, was spending his nights in a mosque. Bhat, a Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commander, was killed in a gunfight on Wednesday morning. After searching most mosques in the area over the last two days, police shifted their focus to the Devsar area of Kulgam on Tuesday. They finally reached Zanglipora. A local villager was sent into the mosque to check if there was anyone inside, and he found a door in the attic bolted from the inside. items.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday chaired a meeting of the council of ministers and underscored the need for a concerted campaign to eradicate drug use, said people aware of the details. According to a person privy to the meeting, the PM expressed concern over the widespread social evil and said drug addiction had emerged as a major challenge for the country. He said just as the government took stern measures against left-wing terrorism and managed to pull out millions from poverty, there was a need to act against drug abuse, this person added. “The prime minister was overcome with emotions when he spoke about the impact drugs use has on the younger demographic and said the social evil needs to be eradicated and no effort must be spared to do so...” said the person quoted above. The Union government has sharpened its campaign against drug abuse, particularly in poll-bound Punjab. items.text: A view of Panjab University in Chandigarh. The University’s overall score has increased to 55.0 from 52.8 in 2026 and 48.6 in 2025. In a statement on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Vice-Chancellor Meenakshi Goyal said, “This improvement in Panjab University’s global standing reflects our continued commitment to strengthening interdisciplinary research and academic collaboration. It is the outcome of the collective efforts of our faculty, researchers, students, and staff. items.text: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Wednesday arrested a key accused – linked to the banned Khalistan Zindabad Force (KZF) terror outfit – in the April 26 Punjab railway line blast case after his deportation from the US. “Surinder Singh alias Thikriwal was detained by the US authorities and deported in coordination with them. Thikriwal was arrested at the IGI airport in the case related to the blast on the railway line of the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Ltd (DFCCIL) between Shambhu and Rajpura stations…,” a NIA spokesperson said. The blast was carried out to further the terror activities of the KZF, disrupt communal harmony and destabilise law and order in Punjab, the probe agency said. With this, the NIA has so far arrested eight accused in the case. During the investigation, it surfaced that after the blast, Thikriwal posted a video on his Facebook account glorifying the incident. “In the video, he also extended support to the accused behind the criminal conspiracy, including the deceased Jagroop Singh, who died while carrying out the blast. items.text: Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) officially launched in India at midnight on Thursday, marking the end of a wait of more than 13 years since the release of the previous mainline title, GTA V, in September 2013. Players who purchased the digital version of GTA 6 through pre-orders could download the game in advance using the pre-load feature. However, this early download did not grant them immediate access, as the game remained locked until its official release. Even those who had completed the pre-loading process had to wait until midnight on November 19 to start playing. Players may need up to 212GB of available storage to install GTA 6, although the exact requirement varies by console. The game is currently available only on consoles, as Rockstar Games has yet to release the PC version or provide a confirmed launch date for it. In India, GTA 6 is being offered in two versions: Standard and Ultimate editions. items.headline: Armed robbers loot jewellery worth more than ₹30 crore at gunpoint in Bihar’s Bettiah
items.blurb: According to the police, eight robbers arrived at the jewellery shop on three motorcycles and seized the mobile phone and then tied their hands.
items.text: Armed robbers looted jewellery worth more than ₹30 crore at gunpoint on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) in broad daylight in Bettiah, the district headquarters of West Champaran, Bihar. The loot is seen as one of the biggest heists in recent times. According to the police, eight robbers arrived at the jewellery showroom on three motorcycles, seized mobile phones, and then tied the hands of the victims. The robber also hit two staff members, including a security guard, with a gun, leaving them injured. A woman staff member, while speaking to local media, said that before leaving the showroom with the looted jewellery, one robber said, “This is just the trailer; the film is yet to come. We will return.” The owner of the jewellery showroom is Brajesh Kushwaha, a leader of the ruling Janata Dal (United). The incident took place at Senco Gold and Diamonds, located near Supriya Cinema Road, under the jurisdiction of Kali Bagh police station. items.headline: Failed attempt, forest ambush and a murder: Odisha trader killed over money dispute, teacher on the run
items.text: A financial dispute took a chilling turn in Odisha’s Boudh district, ending in the murder of a 31-year-old trader. The body of Birupakhya Agrawal, with his throat slit, was recovered from a forest along the Boudh-Sambalpur border on Tuesday, five days after he went missing. Though the police arrested three persons in connection with the crime, the alleged mastermind, Swadhin Pradhan, a teacher, is still at large. The investigation so far has revealed an alleged conspiracy hatched by Pradhan and his associates to eliminate Agarwal over a financial dispute stemming from previous dealings. Barely a week before the murder, the accused, as per police, made an earlier attempt on his life but failed. Boudh Superintendent of Police Kuldeep Meena said technical surveillance helped them zero in on the accused. “After we came to know about the suspects, we first arrested one and subsequently managed to apprehend all three persons, who confessed,” said Meena. items.blurb: JPMORGAN
items.text: Judge says case should be pursued in court, not the media Rana said former colleague coerced him into sex; she countersued for defamation NEW YORK, Nov 18 (Reuters) - JPMorgan Chase failed on Wednesday to win the dismissal of a sexual harassment and discrimination lawsuit by former investment banker Chirayu Rana after accusing him of persuading his sister and a friend to lie for him. US District Judge Lewis Kaplan in Manhattan also exhorted Rana, JPMorgan and co-defendant Lorna Hajdini, a JPMorgan executive, to press their claims and defenses through the court process, lamenting how the case "has been fought in part as a public relations battle." JPMorgan spokesperson Brian Marchiony declined to comment. Lawyers for Hajdini and Rana did not immediately respond to requests for comment. In court papers, Rana accused Hajdini in graphic terms of sexual harassment, including by allegedly coercing him into sex and demanding submissiveness to advance his career. He also accused JPMorgan of destroying his career by tolerating sexual coercion and racism, such as by doing nothing when colleagues called him "brown boy."

items.headline: Foreign Holdings of US Treasuries Decline by Most Since March
items.blurb: Foreign holdings of US Treasuries fell in September by the most in six months, led by decreases in the stockpiles of China and France.
items.text: Foreign holdings of US Treasuries fell in September by the most in six months, led by decreases in the stockpiles of China and France. Overseas holdings dropped by $75.5 billion from August, according to data published by the Treasury Department. The total now stands at $9.24 trillion, the lowest in a year. The foreign holdings data incorporate changes in valuation as well as net sales and purchases. The Bloomberg US Treasury index slumped by 2.2% in September, when the Federal Reserve began a new cycle of interest-rate hikes to temper inflation. Japan, the biggest foreign holder of Treasuries, saw a $5.2 billion drop in its holdings, to $1.063 trillion, the lowest since the end of 2024. Japanese officials were intervening over the summer in the foreign-exchange market, buying yen amid a slump in the currency to its weakest in four decades against the dollar. Japanese data have suggested Tokyo sold a portion of its holdings of Treasuries and other securities to fund such intervention. items.headline: Typical energy bill forecast to go up by £443 a year from January as inflation rate rises again
items.blurb: Energy bills are expected to jump by 26% a year for a typical household as UK inflation hits its highest rate for a year.
items.text: Gas and electricity bills for a typical household are forecast to jump by £443 a year from January as the inflation rate rose to its highest level in a year. A typical annual bill is predicted to rise by 26% in the new year, according to consultancy Cornwall Insight, ahead of the official announcement next week. Some households will get a £100 payment to help with the rising cost of living, a policy which was announced in the Budget. Prices rose 3.6% in the year to October, up from 3.5% in September mainly because of higher petrol and diesel prices, official figures show. Inflation has been driven higher in recent months as the US-Israel war with Iran has driven up the cost of energy and fuel. In response to prices surging, the Bank of England raised interest rates for the first time in three years earlier this month, in a bid to slow inflation to its target of 2%. items.headline: Sell-Side Analysts Rip Short-Seller Report on Retailer Dynamite
items.blurb: Several financial analysts fended off a negative report from short-seller Spruce Point Capital Management LLC about fast-fashion retailer Groupe Dynamite Inc.
items.text: (Bloomberg) -- Several financial analysts fended off a negative report from short-seller Spruce Point Capital Management LLC about fast-fashion retailer Groupe Dynamite Inc. Spruce Point said Tuesday that it’s short the stock, citing potential downside of 35% to 70%. Its report questioned Dynamite’s relationship with a “key Bangladesh supplier,” as well as the retailer’s store-opening targets and inventory turnover amid “weakening momentum with its core customers.” Other concerns were raised related to financial reporting. Shares of Dynamite rose as much as 2% on Wednesday in Toronto after plunging 12% to C$49.83 in the previous session. “We view the selloff as overdone,” Bank of Montreal analyst Stephen MacLeod wrote in a client note. “We believe the report’s conclusions reflect alternative interpretations of operating and financial data rather than evidence of fundamental business issues.” The Montreal-based retailer went public in November 2024, and had surged more than 350% to C$97.45 on April 20 before declining. items.headline: The sandpaper plot - who was there, who said what?

items.text: The sandpaper scandal, one of the biggest controversies in the history of Test cricket, continues to engulf Australian sport. In a detailed account of more than 4,000 words published in the West Australian newspaper, Bancroft alleges all the Australia players and coaches present in Cape Town eight years ago knew of the plot. Bancroft's explosive testimony supports claims made by Usman Khawaja, David Warner and Chadd Sayers. However, Cummins denied Khawaja's version of events in his own extraordinary news conference in Sydney last week. Cummins spoke to the media for 68 minutes in an address broadcast on live television. Here, BBC Sport collects the most recent accounts of players and coaches involved in the saga that became widely known as sandpapergate. items.headline: India win toss, opt to field against New Zealand in opening Test
items.blurb: Gill had no hesitation in making the most of the conditions that have traditionally aided pace bowlers on the first two days of a Test match
items.text: Captain Shubman Gill with New Zealand captain Tom Latham during the toss in Wellington. Photo: X/@BCCI. Shubman Gill’s love affair with calling tails and winning the toss continued as the India captain had no hesitation in opting to field in the first Test against New Zealand on a breezy and sunny morning at the Basin Reserve. Yet to lose a toss on the tour, Gill had no hesitation in making the most of the conditions that have traditionally aided pace bowlers on the first two days of a Test match. While Mohammed Siraj, as expected, missed the cut with India opting to deepen the batting order with pacers who can contribute with the willow, Ravindra Jadeja was benched with the team management preferring Washington Sundar as the lone pacer. As a result, India’s four pacers are Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj. New Zealand, meanwhile, has stuck with the same XI it had announced on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). items.headline: The tightest survival scrap for years? Why it's not too early to worry
items.blurb: The Premier League resumes on Saturday with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Man Utd in the relegation zone. But is it too early to be worried?
items.text: Despite being only 10 games into the season, sitting in the relegation zone even at this early stage is more worrying than you might think. But with how tight the Premier League table is, this could also be one of the fiercest relegation battles we have seen in a long time. Two of the current bottom three, Crystal Palace and Manchester United , will resume their campaigns at the weekend with new managers after appointing Thomas Frank and Mauricio Pochettino respectively. Sunderland , wedged between the pair in 19th, have not pressed the panic button and have kept faith with Regis le Bris. But is it too early to worry? We look at what the stats tell us about relegation battles in the past and what we can learn for the months ahead. Looking at every Premier League season since it changed to a 20-team league in 1995–96, the current bottom three have cause to be concerned. items.text: New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0–1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1–0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. items.text: Like a nasty rash, AI seems to spread everywhere. Google crams AI Overviews down your throat even though it costs the company billions of dollars in lost ad revenue. Leave your apartment, and you might pass two people heaving an AI-powered humanoid robot up the stairs to clean someone’s rooms. Go to the supermarket, and perhaps you’ll slip on a pool of melted ice cream congealing on the floor thanks to an AI-assisted cyberattack . You go to the movies and see Sam Altman being played with nauseating intensity by Andrew Garfield, and go back home to find that Elon Musk has released a Grok-fied version of The Odyssey . You try to watch it, but it feels like a long, unskippable mobile ad. In a way, the whole world kind of feels that way now: Like a modern Odysseus, you are cursed to roam AI-infested waters, dueling with machine gods and monsters, trying to find your way back to somewhere that feels like home. items.text: The computer gaming world hasn’t heard much from Will Wright ( SimCity , The Sims ) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright’s subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA . Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players’ memories. MyMems , which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright’s previous projects by “turning the simulation inward,” as Wright’s Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning . items.text: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The company’s goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.” “Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.” In the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating

items.headline: Palmer Luckey warns AI-powered cyberattacks are outpacing defenses: ‘It’s time to start running’
items.blurb: The Anduril co-founder says outdated technology is leaving systems vulnerable to a new wave of AI-enabled attacks.
items.text: AI-powered cyberattacks are moving faster than outdated technology systems can defend against them, Palmer Luckey warned at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday. Addressing the recent spate of tech outages, the Oculus founder and Anduril Industries co-founder argued that older systems are struggling to keep pace with the new hacking capabilities enabled by AI and warned it was time to quicken the pace of securing our defenses. “We’re seeing the natural effects of a lot of these advanced AI tools allowing for the creation of various exploits,” he said. While government officials largely attributed the latest set of technical issues to companies rushing to patch their systems to protect against the new vulnerabilities AI has discovered, Luckey focused on the underlying security challenges facing organizations using outdated technology. Luckey explained that U.S. adversaries are currently exploiting the mismatch between new attack capabilities and our defense capabilities. These attacks are being carried out for both strategic and financial reasons, and North Korea was particularly involved, he added. items.headline: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
items.blurb: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint now live inside Copilot; always-on agents are next.
items.text: Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company’s vision for its new “frontier ecosystem,” announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as “the new OS for work.” The announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent’s work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications. The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the company first announced in September. As the founder and CEO of OpenAI, one of the most influential companies of the century, Sam Altman isn’t going to escape the Hollywood treatment, either. In “Artificial,” a biographical comedy-drama opening in theaters on Christmas, the lauded actor Andrew Garfield will portray Altman in a film that chronicles OpenAI’s rise and the internal turmoil that erupted when he was briefly ousted in 2023. “If you had told me 20 years ago that someone was going to make a movie about me, I think that would have struck me as … that would have been a very weird thing,” Altman said onstage at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday. “Now it doesn’t feel like it’s in like the top 10

items.headline: Nvidia created a weird bit of intrigue by not filing a routine SEC report
items.blurb: One Wall Street analyst got to the bottom of Nvidia's surprise announcement that it wouldn't be filing its formal quarterly results document, the 10-Q, for weeks.
items.text: During Nvidia’s quarterly call on Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim-CEO Colette Kress dropped this little oddity: She said Nvidia wouldn’t be immediately filing its quarterly results report, known as a 10-Q, with the SEC. “We plan to file our 10-Q in the coming weeks.” And she offered no reason why. The delay was widely noticed. Among the many comments on X about it , economic, and investment analyst Edward Dowd called it a “red flag.” Nvidia has typically filed the 10-Q the same day it reports results. The 10-Q offers far more detail about a company’s operations than an earnings press release, including sections that disclose “legal proceedings,” which include lawsuits that could affect the company; and “risk factors” which cover other potentially business-impairing items. The announcement of the delay was so unusual that UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri asked about it after the public earnings call. items.text: If someone handed you $8,300 every second, what would you do? That’s how much pure profit Nvidia now makes. By the time you finish reading this paragraph, Nvidia will likely have cleared $45,000 and change. It’s easy to look at Nvidia, a company that just lost its visionary founder CEO due to a series of scandals , and think that the company and maybe the entire AI industry are in terrible trouble. Perhaps so ? But I want you to understand: Nvidia isn’t your average semi-successful company that might tempt a new CEO to fix things that are broken. It is a company so staggeringly, mind-bogglingly successful it’ll do everything in its power not to rock the boat. There is so much money at stake. It’s so much money that when I heard about Jensen Huang’s resignation, my first thought was: I need a way to visualize this jaw-dropping amount of money for you . I want to show you that Nvidia has risen so far, so fast, that rival chipmakers AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm barely qualify as competition now.

items.text: On Friday, a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia began circulating on social media, and by Monday it listed some notable signatories, including Elon Musk and several influential Nvidia researchers. But comb through the more than 115,000 names and you’ll notice a significant faction of Huang’s supporters—higher-ups from Hugging Face, a hub for sharing AI models, and venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital—come from a particular slice of the tech world. These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. Supporters of such models say that concentrating AI in the hands of a few powerful companies will leave everyone else worse off (a concern that wouldn’t sound out of place among the AI industry's critics on the left, if so many open-source advocates weren’t also venture capitalists who stand to profit when startups can build on cheaper AI without paying Big Tech). items.text: Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey thinks Nvidia’s board is giving China exactly what it wants by removing the company’s longtime CEO and co-founder, Jensen Huang. Nvidia, the leading semiconductor designer whose chips power much of the AI industry, is undergoing a critical, unexpected leadership change. Huang, who led the company for 33 years, stepped down last week amid several controversies , including his extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy who has been investigated for possibly smuggling Nvidia chips into China to circumvent U.S. export restrictions. “China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said onstage at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, repeating a statement he posted on X last week. “They’re thrilled to have Jensen out… There’s a reason it’s knocking a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market cap. They know it makes America weaker to knock him out.” Luckey disagrees with Huang’s longstanding position that Nvidia should have more leeway to export chips to China. items.text: Anthropic has reportedly priced its long-awaited IPO at $83 per share, above its initial range of $70 to $78, signaling strong investor appetite for one of the companies at the center of the AI boom, despite market jitters following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which shook confidence in the industry. At the IPO price, Anthropic is reportedly valued at $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, a significant increase from the $965 billion the company reached in May when it raised $65 billion in its last private market backers set to round , but below the $2 trillion it was reportedly aiming for several months ago. Anthropic will begin its life as a public company on Thursday, trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol “ANT.” A strong first day of trading would signal that investors remain optimistic about AI adoption, despite recent volatility in AI-driven stocks. items.text: As AI assistants challenge traditional online discovery and reshape user interactions, startups face a new battle for visibility, customer engagement and revenue in an agent-driven internet. In the web era, we operated and connected through distinct platforms, each catering to a specific user need. Search engines were for information, social networks for people, marketplaces for shopping and messaging apps for conversations. But AI assistants have begun to disrupt it all, including the web itself. Today, anyone looking for a new phone may no longer need to search Google, review websites or compare products across multiple tabs. Instead, they can turn to an AI assistant to evaluate options, compare prices and get personalised recommendations. The next stop for AI assistants could very well be social media platforms that have long controlled online discovery through their proprietary algorithms. As AI increasingly takes over product discovery, recommendations and decision-making, platforms that depend on search traffic, user attention and algorithmic distribution could find their influence under threat.
